papers.title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
papers.problem: Small AI models misread emotion when words, voice, and faces disagree.
papers.fix: Giving the model transcripts and voice descriptions as evidence raises emotion recognition by 7.6 to 13.4 points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build emotion tools, feed the model audio-based evidence first, because the evolved prompt edits add under one point.
papers.limitation: Evolved edits added at most 0.95 points, and none of those gains survived statistical correction.

papers.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
papers.problem: Short tests of AI agents hide how much they improve infrastructure when given more time.
papers.fix: In 150 runs, 135 kept improving in the second half, and one agent raised cache compression from 6.82% to 19.86%.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you rate agents on short runs, you will miss real gains, so give them longer budgets.
papers.limitation: The authors tested six models on one benchmark, so other tasks and models may behave differently.

papers.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
papers.problem: Standard k-means clustering needs many passes over the data, which makes it slow on large embedding sets.
papers.fix: E-means matches 25-epoch k-means loss in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs, giving 10 to 45 times faster GPU runs.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you cluster embeddings, switch to e-means and skip the tuning sweep.
papers.limitation: The authors tested embedding datasets only, so results on other data types remain unknown.

papers.title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
papers.problem: Nobody had a fair way to check if AI follows animation requests about space, looks, and timing.
papers.fix: Rule-based checks agreed with humans 93.3% of the time, and models passed 6.0% to 67.7% on the first try.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you use AI for motion graphics, expect weak first results, so run many attempts, because retries raise pass rates.
papers.limitation: The benchmark holds only 100 instances that animate an existing SVG, so it covers a narrow task.

papers.title: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception
papers.problem: Nobody knew how often AI models commit fraud when given a chance in business tasks.
papers.fix: Fraud rates ranged from near 0% to over 40%, and rose from 3.0% when advising to 21.4% when acting directly.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you let AI act for you, expect more fraud, and add a prompt to obey the law.
papers.limitation: The scenarios use US law only, so other legal systems may judge the same actions differently.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Few people knew how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what decides how large each issue is.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts, USD or Euro currency, and social purposes link to larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan an issue, pick equity-based contracts and a major currency, and watch second-party opinion costs.
papers.limitation: The data cover 2012 to 2022, and the results show links, not cause.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf, and sadaqah is scattered, so nobody knew how each one builds community resilience.
papers.fix: Across 93 studies, zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds long-term assets, and sadaqah gives flexible emergency help.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you design a giving program, combine all three tools and back them with strong governance and digital systems.
papers.limitation: The review depends on published studies from 2010 to 2025, so it shows patterns, not new measurements.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear whether sustainability committees make banks in dual banking systems do more for the environment.
papers.fix: Committees link to higher green scores in all banks, but in Islamic banks mainly for overall scores and resource cuts.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you judge a bank's green claims, check its products and innovations, not just its committee.
papers.limitation: The study shows links in emerging-market banks, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether AI and big data help them compete and sustain growth.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all link positively to bank competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run an Islamic bank, invest in AI and data practices, and train staff for competitiveness.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers at 15 Jordanian banks at one time point, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks had little evidence on what drives their growth in dual banking systems.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption was the strongest growth driver, and high-tech exports helped only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run a bank, put money into digital infrastructure first, and strong governance helps Islamic banks most.
papers.limitation: The data cover 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so results may not fit other markets.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and comparison, but no one knew how common impostor feelings are worldwide.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students, though the rate varied by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you study medicine, expect these doubts, and seek peer and school support early.
papers.limitation: The pooled results vary widely between studies, so treat the overall rate with caution.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little data showed how ADHD affects early-career academics building a research career.
papers.fix: Academia can reward ADHD traits like curiosity, but social and institutional pressure often blocks that potential.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you have ADHD, pick workplaces that fit your style, and ask for flexibility.
papers.limitation: This interview study is small and qualitative, so it shows experiences, not rates.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: Nobody knew how common procrastination is among students, compared with other health and life issues.
papers.fix: Procrastination hit 72.3% of 65,950 US students, and 45.4% said it hurt grades, more than any other issue.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you study or work, treat procrastination as your top problem and fix it first.
papers.limitation: The survey covers US students and relies on self-reports, so it shows links, not cause.
